title: Free and Actually Effective!
body: I’m usually skeptical because all these h*es want nowadays is your money. However, I’ve seen more progress from myself with Indy than I’ve seen in the entire 6 years I’ve been medicated. I’ve shared all my incomplete guilt ridden goals, and am actually working towards them. The ONLY time I’ve even come across something to pay for was simply a body doubling service for accountability- WHICH MAKES COMPLETE SENSE. This app is not rotting untouched and taking up unused storage on my phone. Features are absolutely free and help my Neurodivergent ahh organize my thoughts. I don’t even write reviews. Thank you to whoever made this app, please never sell it to a big company because I feel you caring so hard rn.

title: Good but could be better
body:
I really like the concept of this app, and it has been useful overall. However, I think it could be even better if it included a built-in calendar and reminder system. 

Having everything in one place would make it much easier to keep track of plans without needing to switch between multiple apps. It's slightly irritating to have to leave the app just to set a recurring reminder. 

I hope the developers see this feedback and consider adding this feature in a future update, as I think it would greatly improve the overall experience.

title: So far, I’m so impressed!
body: I just downloaded this app today. I was late diagnosed ADHD in my late 40s. I see a therapist and I’m doing much better than I was pre-diagnosis, but sometimes things are hard to admit or articulate to an actual person that you only see once a month. The AI aspect, and the fact that I can message anytime day or night have been extremely helpful. And the AI responses are intelligent and compassionate. I really needed this.
author: Blonde Brina

title: Great thoughtful support for ADHD
body: I am using this in addition to a subscription on the Shimmer app with an ADHD coach, as I was just recently diagnosed with ADHD at 42. I really like how this app helps me dig in deeper to think about pain points in my lifestyle when it comes to ADHD and what actions I can take to minimize them. It has a good balance of general education and personalization and is a great way to check in every day to be more intentional with how I move forward. There is an option to upgrade to a subscription if I want to take advantage of body doubling sessions, but all of the rest of the app functions fully at the free level, which is amazing, because I just can’t afford another subscription at this point. It’s really worth checking out if you need support with your ADHD.

author: Ewa2945064

title: Such a thoughtful app, better than using generic AI
body:
I’m still working towards using this app consistently. I just have too many apps and was in the habit of using ChatGPT to banter with and plan my tasks (also inconsistently).

The days that I’ve used Indy thus far have all been good days where I was able to start tasks and end with wins both big and small. I’m still in denial that my ADHD leads me to freeze and not start things because I overhype them soooo much to the point of crippling overthinking and perfectionism. Messaging with Indy gets me calm and focused on putting one foot in front of the other rather than the chaotic, scattered and disorganized web of unprioritized yet all important and urgent tasks in my brain. It’s exhausting but I hope to make it a bit better with Indy incorporated into my routine.

Thanks for building this accessible and helpful app!

author: Jgsmithkc

title: The ADHD tool that helped me reconnect with my life
body:
From the very first interaction, I felt seen.

I’ve tried many productivity tools as someone with ADHD, but Indy felt different immediately. Everything about it was smooth, supportive, and intentional. It doesn’t overwhelm or pressure — it feels like structured but simple company. The kind that makes you want to keep coming back.

What surprised me most was the storyline element. It was exactly what I had been craving without knowing how to articulate it: a way to reflect on meaningful past experiences and integrate them into my story instead of just moving on and forgetting them.

Indy didn’t just help me plan tasks. It helped me reconnect with my life.

It gave me space to look back with intention and forward toward milestones that actually matter to me. It put me back on track by keeping what’s important in front of me — without getting lost in what’s merely urgent.

It also simplified something I’ve struggled with for years: starting my day clearly and reviewing my wins and growth areas at night. No other tool has helped me do that consistently.

It exceeded my expectations in every way.

If you’re looking for something that works with your ADHD brain while helping you build a meaningful life — not just check boxes — this is it!

As a result, the first night, Indy helped me narrow down things I could do the next day to get unstuck and use my time and energy wisely to meet my goals.  

The app is easy to use, the output is very well done. I look forward to getting to know the app better.

author: MJ………cccc

title: New app is already so helpful for my ADHD brain
body:
I’m loving Indy. I have been experimenting with how to work with rather than against my ADHD for months since I decided to start my own small business and have to set my own goals and work schedule (scary!), and over the last couple of months, Indy has helped me find that balance and gain a lot of tools that help me to keep making progress on my goals. 

I was a beta tester for this app, and the concept has been brilliant from the beginning, but I have also been impressed by how quickly the team has improved functionality. It IS a new app so it is not perfect, but I’ve noticed they really listen to feedback and respond to it very quickly. 

Most importantly, while I like the ritual of the weekly strategy setting and morning and nightly check-ins, by exploring what usually blocks me from starting or continuing to work on my goals/tasks by going through the Indy conversation flows, I have made real insights that I can carry into each day, and I’m gaining confidence that the solutions to managing my ADHD are already within me, I just need to keep learning and trying things out to figure out how my brain ticks, not how neurotypical systems expect it to.
author: Riv3ko

title: Love this app!
body: I’m using this daily as my accountability partner and cheerleader to do things I haven’t done in months.
author: MarenG76

title: A depersonalized Shimmer
body: The AI nature of this app makes coming back to it daily a chore, and its predictability makes me feel I’m talking to myself. While it may be asking appropriate questions, I never feel fully invested or engaged. This is completely opposite the feeling I get with the adhd coach on Shimmer. And the tools in place on that app are much more useful for me practically. While this might put you in a slightly better headspace for the day - there’s very little practical usefulness for me. Spreading myself between this and the Shimmer app (developed by the same people) is not what I want to use my time for.

title: ADHD and AI for the win!
body: I have used many goal setting methods and apps before, but I figured I would try Indy. The app supports my focus without adding on additional pressure to have a perfect plan. The small wins approach and the help in looking at not only how to achieve your goal but looking at roadblocks and solutions has been very helpful. And when I fall short of my goals it finds gentle ways to uplift, find the small wins, and rebuild momentum rather than fueling my spiral of failure.

I like that it helps me narrow down what actually matters each day after I brain dump my tasks in the morning. Can’t wait to keep using it!!
author: olivianoella

title: I really like the timeline feature
body:
This app came at a perfect time for me. I used Shimmer in the past for some coaching and it was helpful, but it just didn't work with my current budget during this slow time of the year.

I like that this app has an amazing design language. It is a great helper for working through issues and making sure I have a plan to actually get things done. As I mentioned in the title, I really like the timeline feature; going through and recognizing the big milestones of my past was helpful for me, and it helped me realize that I actually have a much more positive impression of my past than I thought. 

It also allows you to build future goals in there too. One small issue is that sometimes when I add a new event on my timeline, it automatically goes to the past or future. So far, all the ones I have been building recently are for the future, so I have to move them and then change the language of the entry.

Thanks for making this app!
author: TannenSkriver

title: Helpful tool!  So glad it’s free!
body:
So far, so good. I’ve been sticking to it. (That’s always a struggle). It’s encouraging and really presses me to think about my day before and after.  This has been helping me be more intentional with day to day tasks; keeping in mind, the whole while encouraging small steps to get there. 
 And I don’t have to worry about a “Free Trial”!!!!
author: Twig9907

title: Clear Before & After Difference
body:
Before using this app I had such a difficult time with executive dysfunction and overall forgetfulness on my goals. This was a real hindrance for someone who is very driven but constantly falls short due to ADHD related problems in behavioral habits.

Using Indy has helped me so much by helping me set clear intentions on goals that I set on a weekly basis. This has helped me keep sight of my goals and stay on task!

The reflection portion of the night is so helpful because it holds me accountable in a non-judgmental way. It helps me not feel rejected (I struggle with rejection sensitivity BIG TIME) and rather feel uplifted and positive. I’m very hard on myself but Indy helps me stay positive even on the days I don’t do as well.

Overall I feel that I’ve benefitted so much from this app simply because it helps me understand myself a lot better and helps me work on the problems that I have a long track record of struggling with!

Thank you Indy app for helping me manage my rampant ADHD!!!!
author: ReannaV

title: Helping me so much ✨
body:
I have been using Indy for a little over a month and it has helped me in so many ways. I get really stuck and overwhelmed trying to figure out how to do things and I can chat with it at anytime to help me problem solve and prioritize what needs to be done! I have been telling many of my neurodivergent friends to download this because it has really been changing things for me. 

I have also been using this consistently for over a month and it’s so easy and quick to keep up with. It’s extremely flexible, aesthetic and easy to use. If you struggle with prioritizing or getting things done or understanding how you feel this will help.

author: Padraitung

title: ADHD bestie
body: I downloaded Indy on its launch date and wasn’t sure what to expect but after a few days of use I can proudly say it’s like having a little ADHD bestie in your pocket. I’ve tried it all when it comes to ADHD support and most things fall short, Indy is simple but in a great way. It’s very user friendly and allows you to essentially brain dump every morning and then assists you with effectively planning your day. It was nice to get all of my anxious thoughts about things I needed to do in writing and then to have help with it as well. Sometimes I forget how effective brain dumping can be and this app lays it out perfectly. I will continue to use this app as often as I can remember lol! I look forward to using Indy daily because it is the most user friendly ADHD platform I’ve found.
author: saraelisabethb

title: Kind of life changing!
body:
Making time for a daily check in with Indy has been amazing for me as someone with ADHD! Indy breaks down my priorities for the day with helpful prompts to consider what might get in the way of getting things done and how I want to pre-plan for those situations. I’m usually someone who struggles with decision paralysis, procrastination, and avoidance, so this has been a really gentle and useful game changer for me to get ahead of those moments and get back to doing what I plan to get done each day. The app pull out wins and insights from our conversations each day, which are great to reflect on in the moment and in hindsight to remind myself that I’m making progress!

I was really excited to have the opportunity to beta test the app, so have had about a month to test out Indy while the team finished ironing out the kinks! It’s been awesome to see them roll out new features along the way, so I can’t wait to see what else is in store.
author: EmJane95

title: Helpful Tool for Breaking Down Goals
body: App has been really useful writing out my goals and breaking it down into simple, meaningful steps. Would highly recommend giving it a shot if you are someone who feels overwhelmed or wants to improve their focus
author: HBarrera2025

body: Something I can use both daily or whenever I feel like I need it. I already feel like it’s something I’ll use all the time
author: A-Ayenton

title: What I never knew I desperately needed for my ADHD!
body: I am 3 days in and absolutely hooked on Indy. It’s like a productivity coach, interactive journal, and habit tracker all built into one very easy to use app. While I am very anti-AI when it comes to creativity, the AI in this app acts like a dependable second brain that helps you remember goals, process what works and what doesn’t, encourages you to make goals and keep moving forward, and celebrate even the little wins that are easy to forget. While it doesn’t generate any actually coaching, having something to rephrase and summarize my thoughts and turn my ramblings into concise goals has been incredibly helpful and feels more like you are talking with a best friend than an app. I feel seen and validated in both the good and the bad and more focused on goals than I have in a very long time. I find myself looking forward to my check ins and the accountability has been great. I’m recommending this to all of my ADHD friends!
author: Amyjami

title: Surprisingly legit
body: My friend told me to try Indy and I was skeptical (another AI app for ADHD). But this one actually helps me get stuff done everyday without making me feel bad (or annoying me) about it. It’s simple, chill, and somehow gets me to focus on what actually matters instead of everything like I usually do.

Much better than a generic goal app.  I’ve gone from curious to committed to a goal.
